A1.justification: The title, method, central equations and main experiments clearly match. However, v4 ends after the references despite citing appendices, whereas v6 includes Appendices A–H. The main text is directly comparable; supplementary additions below mean newly included material in the supplied PDF, not established changes to unseen earlier supplements.

before.justification: Section 6, Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–4 report original classification, missing-modality segmentation, synthetic representation experiments and ablations.

after.justification: v6 retains those original experiments and includes further counterfactual comparisons, robustness tests, feature interventions and efficiency analyses in its appendices.

M1.justification: The attention-based instrumental variable, shared twin network, gradient intervention, KL constraints and C3R objective remain unchanged in Equations 6–10. Algorithm 1 and the appended implementation explanations document the existing procedure without establishing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same six datasets and principal tasks. Appendix H.6 additionally reports NYU Depth V2 evaluation with 30% of the input area masked, extending the reported corruption scenarios beyond the earlier Gaussian/blank noise and missing-modality evaluations.

E2.justification: Tables 6–7 include standalone RGB, Depth, Bow, Img and BERT comparators absent from v4's Table 1. Table 5 also evaluates manually curated and transport-based counterfactual alternatives. The comparator sets in the retained main tables remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Additional evaluation procedures include 30% area masking, frozen-classifier tests that reduce high-weight features or double and normalize low-weight features, and four-way distance-loss comparisons measuring accuracy and training time. These expand the documented evaluation design; the main optimizer and corruption settings remain unchanged. Newly supplied split details do not establish a revised split.

E4.justification: Figures 3–4 retain the original representation analysis and loss-term ablation. The appendices supply additional spurious-correlation conditions, counterfactual-construction comparisons, feature-weight interventions and heatmaps, masking robustness, and distance-loss ablations. Efficiency and parameter-sensitivity analyses mentioned but unavailable in v4 are now included.

E5.justification: v4 already reports five runs and displays boxplots. v6 additionally supplies uncertainty values throughout Tables 6–7. Their captions describe three random runs over 40 randomly selected hyperparameter settings, conflicting with the retained five-run statements in Section 6.1, Table 3 and Appendix G. An actual increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–4 are unchanged, but substantial supplementary results are now supplied. Table 8 reports LCKD+C3R accuracies of 85.39, 83.73 and 84.02 for original, reduced-high-weight and increased-low-weight representations. Table 9 adds masked-input accuracies of 71.26 for MMBT+C3R and 75.49 for QMF+C3R. These are additional conditions, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The main definitions and theorem statements are retained. v6 supplies proof arguments for Theorems 3.2–3.5 and 4.1, additional derivations and formal definitions, and Propositions D.3–D.4 concerning local invertibility and Markov identifiability. This substantially expands the documented mathematics without establishing that the original theorems were corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: causally sufficient and necessary representations, identification without exogeneity and monotonicity, theoretical support for C3 risk, and effective plug-and-play C3R regularization. Additional supporting material does not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: Section 2 qualifies the duck example by its task/data conditions and adds a sufficient-and-necessary duck-bill example. Appendices substantially expand counterfactual mechanism explanations, causal interpretations of feature weights and arguments favoring KL divergence. H.6 also introduces a less-than-2% masking-degradation claim, although Tables 1 and 9 imply drops of 2.48 and 2.09 percentage points.

D1.justification: Beyond v4's brief architecture, optimizer and hardware description, v6 supplies pseudocode, synthetic-data construction and sample counts, benchmark descriptions, validation-based selection, grid-search refinement and backbone details. Section 6.1 adds a code-repository link. These substantially expand disclosed implementation and access information without demonstrating changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: Appendix D.6 broadens the positioning beyond the earlier emphasis on Pearl and Yang et al., explicitly contrasting assumptions, identifiability and objectives with works including Ahuja et al., Yao et al., Sun et al., and Wang and Jordan. Numerous supporting causal, counterfactual and distance-measure references are also added; publication-metadata updates alone do not drive this judgment.

P1.justification: The main section sequence remains stable, but v6 develops extensive explanatory passages and worked examples in an organized A–H supplement with a reading guide and experiment overview. The introduction and duck explanation are refined, causal-identifiability terminology is clarified, and author, affiliation, proceedings and acknowledgement text is updated.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is enlarged, redrawn with textual modality examples and moved to page 2. The appendices introduce the twin-network diagram, expanded uncertainty tables, notation and experiment tables, efficiency and sensitivity plots, heatmaps and additional result tables. Figure 6 combines an additional condition with the retained Figure 3 analysis; the principal tables and Figures 2–4 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v6 substantially improves inspectability through previously unavailable appendices, implementation disclosures and fuller experimental reporting. However, the added support contains consequential problems: Appendix A.1 uses monotonicity to eliminate the necessity event although its stated implication excludes the opposite event; run-count descriptions conflict; and the masking-degradation interpretation contradicts the tables. These gains in completeness coexist with unresolved reliability problems, preventing a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
